original_value: Wi-Fi HaLow is an adaptation of the widespread Wi-Fi technology for the Internet of Things scenarios. Such scenarios often involve numerous wireless stations connected to a shared channel, and contention for the channel significantly affects the performance in such networks. Wi-Fi HaLow contains numerous solutions aimed at handling the contention between stations, two of which, namely, the Centralized Authentication Control (CAC) and the Distributed Authentication Control (DAC), address the contention reduction during the link set-up process. The link set-up process is special because the access point knows nothing of the connecting stations and its means of control of these stations are very limited. While DAC is self-adaptive, CAC does require an algorithm to dynamically control its parameters. Being just a framework, the Wi-Fi HaLow standard neither specifies such an algorithm nor recommends which protocol, CAC or DAC, is more suitable in a given situation. In this paper, we solve both issues by developing a novel robust close-to-optimal algorithm for CAC and compare CAC and DAC in a vast set of experiments.

result.paraphrase: Wi-Fi HaLow adapts the widely used Wi‑Fi technology for Internet of Things use cases. These environments typically feature many wireless stations sharing a common channel, where contention can greatly impact network performance. To address station contention, Wi‑Fi HaLow includes several mechanisms; among them, Centralized Authentication Control (CAC) and Distributed Authentication Control (DAC) focus on reducing contention during link setup. This phase is unique because the access point has no information about the stations that are joining and has only limited control over them. DAC is self-adaptive, whereas CAC requires an algorithm to dynamically manage its parameters. As a framework, the Wi‑Fi HaLow standard does not define such an algorithm or advise whether CAC or DAC is preferable in a given case. In this paper, we address both gaps by designing a new robust near-optimal algorithm for CAC and by comparing CAC and DAC through extensive experiments.
